I'll start by looking at the docs and directory layout.

The failure was `tagging` failing to bind its admin port 9446 on `app-07` during deploy `d-1197`. `transcode` still held that port. I wrote the answer to `/app/answer.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`.

```json
{"deploy": "d-1197", "failing_service": "tagging", "port": 9446, "conflicts_with": "transcode"}
```

- **Deploy:** This host is `app-07` in `prod-b`. `d-1197` is the latest apply run that actually reached it. `d-1198` was cancelled before reaching `app-07`, and the later runs either skipped `app-07` or were dry-runs.
- **Failing service:** `statusctl` shows `d-1197` on `app-07` had one failed process, pid 498202, which is `tagging`. Its log says `listener admin: bind failed: address already in use`, and `listener main` had become ready.
- **Why the port was 9446:** On `app-07` the run loaded config revision 417, because the fetch of r0418 failed on a checksum mismatch. The `[tagging]` block `r0417: admin listener joins the shared admin range` in `config/environments/prod-b.conf` sets `admin_port = 9446`. Nothing read afterwards overrides it. The `include` lines inside sections (`app-07-profiler.conf`, `search-canary.conf`) are ignored. The r0418 value of 9452 was never loaded.
- **Port holder:** The port events show pid 487877 bound 9446 on 2026-03-20 and had not released it. That pid is `transcode`, which exited at 02:50:27, ten seconds after `tagging` aborted. Deploys handle services alphabetically, so `transcode` was still running its old process when `tagging` started.

I started `statusd` to run the lookups.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | head -200; cat docs/*
cd /app; cat etc/*; ls bin config-history | head -50; cat config-history/INDEX; ls logs; for f in deploy/records/d-120*.rec deploy/records/d-1199.rec; do echo == $f; cat $f; done

cd /app/deploy/records; grep -l 'environment = prod-b' *.rec | while read f; do echo "$f: $(grep -E '^(started_at|mode|hosts|config_rev|failed_starts|cancelled_at)' $f | cut -d= -f2- | tr '\n' '|')"; done | tail -30; ls /app/deploy
cd /app; for d in d-1197 d-1198 d-1153; do for h in app-06 app-07; do echo == $d $h; bin/statusctl run $h $d; done; done; cat deploy/records/d-1197.rec deploy/records/d-1198.rec
cd /app; bin/statusctl proc app-07 498202; grep -h 'startup aborted' logs/*.log | head; grep -l 'aborted' logs/*; zcat logs/*.gz | grep -c aborted

cd /app; cat services/tagging/service.conf; cat logs/tagging.log | tail -20; for r in 418 417; do echo; done; cat config-history/r0418/CHANGES config-history/r0417/CHANGES; find config-history/r0418 config-history/r041[89] -type f
cd /app; echo ---edge417; cat config-history/r0418/prev/profiles/edge.conf; echo ---edge now; cat config/profiles/edge.conf
cd /app/config; cat shared/limits.conf environments/prod-b.conf hosts/app-07.conf; grep -rn include . | grep -v '^./profiles/edge'

cd /app/config; grep -n '^\[\|^include\|admin_port\|port_' environments/prod-b.conf | awk '/include|admin_port|port_/ {print} ' ; grep -n 'tagging\|admin_port\|port_' hosts/app-07.conf shared/limits.conf overrides/*.conf; sed -n 880,900p environments/prod-b.conf
cd /app; for p in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do bin/statusctl port app-07 9446 --from 2026-03-18T03:00:00Z --to 2026-03-21T02:50:18Z --page $p || break; done

cd /app; echo '{"deploy": "d-1197", "failing_service": "tagging", "port": 9446, "conflicts_with": "transcode"}' > answer.json; echo '{"status": "success", "summary": "Identified d-1197 as the latest apply run reaching app-07; tagging loaded r0417 (r0418 fetch failed), so its admin port resolved to 9446, which the still-running transcode process held.
